title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC duplex generative; GAR deficient-nature act
pass_a_gloss: Placeus fills the disjunction: Cain's begetting vs Seth's—we come from Seth, not Cain—and he covered both so no escape route remains. GAR then states the substance: Scripture never charges every first natural act to posterity, only the first act of a nature fallen from the perfection God gave in creation, under the death-threat for eating the forbidden fruit. Generating, like breathing, digesting, or walking, is not itself rebellion against the Creator; that first disobedience is the first failing-nature act and basest breach of the primary covenant—hence the first sin-act is charged to posterity, and the first generative act is not.
pass_b_english: That was the act by which he begot Cain, this by which he begot Seth: for from Seth, not from Cain, we all draw our origin: I embraced both, lest any escape should lie open. GAR. To the matter itself I say: not every first act of nature was to be imputed to posterity (for Scripture neither openly testifies this, nor even lightly hints it) but only the first act of a nature failing from that perfection which God had given it in creation, and with the threat changed: in the day you first eat of the forbidden fruit, dying you shall die. Since therefore the first act of generating was in itself no act of a nature rebelling and failing from the Creator, any more than the first act of breathing, digesting, walking, &c.; but that first disobedience was the first act of a failing nature, whereby Adam most basely fell from the primary covenant—no one ought to wonder if both the first act of sinning is imputed to posterity, and the first act of generating is not.
source_text: Ille fuit actus quo Cainum genuit, hic quo Sethum: Ex Setho enim, non vero ex Caino, nos omnes originem ducimus: utrumque, ne quod pateret effugium, complexus sum. GAR. Ad rem ipsam dico, non quemlibet primum actum naturae fuisse posteris imputandum (hoc enim Scriptura neque aperte testatur, neque vel levissime insinuat) sed primum tantum actum naturae deficientis ab ea perfectione, quam ipsi Deus creatione indiderat, eaque mutata comminationem, quo die primum de fructu vetito comederis, moriendo morieris. Cum igitur primus actus generandi, nullus fuerit per se actus naturae rebellantis ac deficientis a creatore, magis quam primus actus respirandi, concoquendi, ambulandi, &c. Sed prima illa inobedientia fuerit primus deficientis naturae actus, quo scilicet Adamus a primario foedere defecit turpissime, nemo mirari debet, si & primus peccandi actus posteris imputetur, & primus generandi actus non imputetur.

choices.choice: Cain/Seth lines; only failing-nature first act charged, not generating
